data.completion_memo: User approved Option A. Portable JSONL/CAS remains the sole canonical semantic history; a strictly noncanonical machine-local SQLite Portable Runtime Journal stores only local binding, frozen-snapshot, approval/input delivery, deduplication, outbox, process-generation, uncertain-outcome, and recovery facts fenced by exact portable commit/head identities. The already-designed two-store sequence remains: prepare portable objects, durably record PendingPortableCommit and operational mutations, publish and freshly verify the portable head, durably finalize HeadLinked, then and only then acknowledge or deliver. Exact same-installation reconciliation of MachineInstanceId, BindingGeneration, ChatId, BranchId, CommitId, verified head, and journal fences resumes the original Chat/Run. Missing/mismatched journal, clone/new machine, stale backup generation, or explicit rebind stays inert/quarantined and creates a new child Chat/Run and portable branch only after fresh local binding, authority, and approvals. Backups cannot transfer identity or authority. Only fully settled terminal/superseded state may compact; pending, uncertain, and quarantined evidence remains protected. Hardened the root system invariant and Portable Runtime Journal absence/retention contract at design revision 69; existing commit/recovery UML and structural design required no change. No source files were created or changed.

lines:
Verify the formal design decision that an active PortableProject Chat may use a strictly noncanonical machine-local Portable Runtime Journal while its semantic history remains canonical only in immutable project JSONL/CAS.

Proposed semantics to confirm:
- The local journal is keyed to the verified portable CommitId/head hash and contains only local binding, full frozen-snapshot, approval/input delivery, deduplication, outbox, process-generation, and recovery facts.
- It is never exported, never a semantic event stream, never authority on another machine, and never permits effect replay.
- Same-machine restart can resume the same non-terminal Chat after exact two-store reconciliation.
- A checkout/import without a matching journal remains inert and requires explicit local capability rebinding and fresh authority. It does not silently continue the old active runtime.
- Terminal/superseded operational state may be compacted only after all pending/uncertain delivery facts are resolved.

Alternatives to discuss:
A. Accept this design (recommended) as compatible with exactly one canonical history.
B. Treat portable history only as inert checkpoints and always create a new child Chat for continuation, revising the concept's same-Run restart promise.
C. Put machine-neutral runtime state into portable records, which would require revisiting the deliberate exclusion of local bindings, approvals, and authority.

Required output: confirm the semantic model, missing-journal behavior, backup/retention expectations, same-machine versus new-machine identity rules, and any wording changes to the root/store contracts.

data.title: Discussion: verify portable same-Run recovery semantics
